title.narrative: Provision of live-saving WASH assistance to the most vulnerable communities in Dinsoor to address impacts of dry conditions and mitigate displacement

description.narrative: ltpgtIn alignment with the May 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan, STS will prioritize the most vulnerable communities in underserved and hard-to-reach areas of Dinsoor. Dinsoor currently faces Level 4 sectoral needs due to rising insecurity, drought-induced displacements, and protection risks, all of which are limiting access to basic services, shelter, and livelihoods.ltbrgtSTS aims to enhance inclusion, reduce protection risks, and improve access to essential WASH services, thereby lowering disease burden and improving health, nutrition, and dignity outcomes. The intervention targets 12,000 individuals (3840 women, 3120 girls, 2400 men 2640 boys), with specific outreach to persons with disabilities across 7 urban villages (Jameeco ,Siinay,Yaqshiid ,Holwadag ,Waberi, Wadajir and Horseed) and 5 IDP Camps (Bilile, Korka MareIDP 2, QotQot IDP, Turwalun IDP 2,Hubey IDP) and 2 rural villages (Towfiq and Buryarow)ltbrgt experiencing extreme WASH needs. The response will draw lessons from recent Islamic Relief WASH interventions to ensure synergies and resource optimization. Interventions will be multisectoral and integrated, thus reducing duplication, improving coordination, and maximizing impact. Activities includelt/pgtltulgtltligtRehabilitation of 2 deep shallow wells (Siinay deep well in Siinay village and Warable deep well in Howlwadaag village)ltbrgtlt/ligtltligtRehabilitation of 5 shallow wells (Arabe, Biyamalow, Ramo Dhabay, Hubey, and Barake Kusow) lt/ligtltligtConstruction of flood proof latrines (50 regular and 8 disability friendly), installation of solar lighting outside the latrines and distribution of sanitation setslt/ligtltligtRehabilitation of 6 Institutional latrines -2 in DMO Health Centre Howlwadaag1 male, 1 female, and 4 in Dinsoor Main Hospital (1 male, 1 female).lt/ligtltligtDistribution of 800 Hygiene kitslt/ligtltligtChlorination of 10 community water sources lt/ligtltligtTraining 77 WASH Committee members, drawn from the communities around the rehabilitated water infrastructuresltbrgtlt/ligtltligtTraining of project staff and contractors on PSEAlt/ligtltligt25 hygiene promotion sessionslt/ligtltligtTrain 15 hygiene promoters drawn from the target villageslt/ligtltligtSanitation toolkits and core WASH kits will be distributed, alongside key training sessions (e.g., PSEA, hygiene promotion, water management).lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtThe intervention adopts a gender-sensitive and protection-focused approach. Priority will be given to female-headed households, pregnant/lactating women, and persons with disabilities. WASH infrastructure will be designed with protection considerations: gender-separated latrines with lockable doors, adequate lighting, and accessible water points within safe distances.ltbrgtInclusion will be operationalized through participatory community engagement processes that ensure the views of women, youth, persons with disabilities, and minority clans are reflected in needs assessments, design, and implementation. STS will recruit and train local mobilizers and hygiene promoters fairly, to include women and PWDs, to foster trust, ownership, and accessibility. Specific consultation sessions with vulnerable groups has informed location and design of infrastructure, ensuring practical usability and safety.ltbrgtCommunity priorities, especially from marginalized groups, will be integrated into project planning and implementation. A tailored CFM will ensure responsiveness to local needs and continuous improvement, with multiple reporting channels—including focal persons from vulnerable groups—ensuring accessibility and feedback loops.ltbrgtTo strengthen convergence and coordination, project staff will actively engage in WASH, FSL, Health, and Protection cluster meetings, inter-cluster forums, and government coordination platforms at both state and regional levels. These forums will support harmonized. implementation, peer learning, and avoidance of overlap. Priority will be placed on sustainable infrastructure development in IDP settlements, schools, health facilities, and nutrition centers—enhancing resilience and long-term service access for disaster-affected populations.ltbrgtlt/pgt
